problem: Given that $x=-10$ is a solution to the equation ${x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-24x+160=0,$ find the remaining solutions.

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Cubic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+100x+25.$ Since $x=-\frac{1}{4}$ is a root of $f(x),$ then according to the factor theorem $(x+\frac{1}{4})$ is a factor of $f(x).$ 

We find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+\frac{1}{4})$ using synthetic division.

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{4}$ | $4$ | $1$ | $100$ | $25$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $-25$ |
|  | $4$ | $0$ | $100$ | $0$ |

Thus, $f(x)=(x+\frac{1}{4})(4{x}^{2}+100).$ 

To find the remaining two roots, we solve $4{x}^{2}+100=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+100 & =0 \\ 4{x}^{2} & =-100 \\ {x}^{2} & =-25 \\ {x}^{2} & =(5\text{i})^{2} \\ x & =\pm 5\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are $x=-\frac{1}{4},\,\pm 5\text{i}.$
